Creordics

creo, ordo, -ics
Every action alters the informational structure of its environment, and unavoidably produces entropy. Some actions create new patterns that other systems can build upon—this is what we call “meaning.” The morality of an action is defined by the quality and persistence of order it enables across systems. The most moral actions are those that propagate meaningful structure, allowing life to act more meaningfully in the future.
Thus, creordics: the study of ethical, meaningful, order-creating actions.
Some of the questions it aims to answer:
  • What is the purpose of life?
  • What is the ideal government?
  • How can we protect humanity from unbounded AI?
  • How can the religious and non-religious coexist peacefully?
  • What should I do with my life?
Creordics is ambitious, and seeks to embrace the academic community for its scientific justification, while enthralling the general public to maximize its impact. Its current status is nascent, in which the core concepts are being developed and strengthened.
